messages:
sam: Deploys to prod are failing on the gha-runner job 'release/publish' after we tightened service account scopes yesterday. Getting 403s with 'insufficient_scope' from the token exchange. Anyone seen this?

maya: Which job run / pipeline id? Logs?

sam: Here is the job snippet (from GH Actions runner):

```
2026-03-16T09:12:34Z runner: POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/models/generate -> 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"Service account token does not have required tokenCreator scope"}
```

sam: It started immediately after the SA scope hardening PR (#4123).

alex: Probable cause: CI's impersonation principal lost roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target CI service account. We removed a broad binding and replaced it with tighter perms but maybe left out tokenCreator.

maya: Can repro locally by impersonating the SA from my laptop. Steps:
1) gcloud auth login --brief
2) gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate --impersonate-service-account=redwood-ci-deployer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --command="curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health"

Result: 403 with same insufficient_scope payload.

sam: We briefly rolled back the scope change and the deploy succeeded. So it's definitely permissions-related, not a token TTL.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0316-07 (automated) - created in incidents queue.

support-esc: Tagging platform-team. We should capture minimal repro and a fix plan (temporary rollback vs. scoped restore). Also note audit log entries for iam.bindings to trace which binding removal caused this.

alex: Quick mitigation if you need a hotfix: re-grant tokenCreator to the CI principal with the least-privilege binding:

```bash
# grant impersonation right to CI runner service account (least-privilege)
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding redwood-ci-deployer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

alex: Longer-term: use Workload Identity / short-lived SA impersonation with IAM Conditions limiting by workload name or audience. That way you don't need broad org-level bindings.

maya: Question on least-privilege: can we scope the role to only allow token creation for specific audiences (the GH Actions audience) or specific method calls?

alex: You can use IAM Conditions to limit by resource.name or by attributes (e.g., 'request.auth.aud' in the condition) depending on provider. For GCP SA tokenCreator you can add a condition that checks request.time and principal, see example in infra runbook. If we need, I'll draft the condition.

support-esc: Action items:
- sam: confirm rollback window and keep logs (done)
- alex: apply temporary add-iam-policy-binding to unblock prod (approved by eng manager)
- maya: run repro after fix and paste sanitized logs here
- platform-team: prepare a safe scoped IAM Condition policy and propose in PR

sam: applying the temporary binding now, will report back after pipeline kick.

(more later)

sam: update: after adding the tokenCreator binding the release/publish job succeeded. Will follow up with audit entries and PR to reintroduce a scoped binding. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks. Please include the exact gcloud command and the audit log entry (who changed what) in the follow-up so security can sign off.

alex: Will open PR with IAM Condition example and a runbook step for future hardenings.

support-esc: Closing triage for now, leaving follow-up tasks in platform backlog.
